pages.text: 5£ on way home by July 20, 1945 Creighton's predicament. Adame betting that won't be home by then. Fighting will cease in November. 1£ Creighton. 1£ to 1/2£ that U.S. landings on P.I. by Sept 15 Luck. Jones 5£ that will be home in 18 months. 1£ with Creighton that no landing on Philippine will be made in Sept., 1944.

pages.title: Overseas Voyage & Life in New Guinea
pages.text: Sea Sickness. Scare about sub. Cape Mendocino, David W. Hewes [New]. P.X. at Brisbane, Moresby & Gusap. Buzzing of planes, Accident at Mess Hall Mar 4. 3 stoves exploded. Same day two P-39. crash. V-mail Free. no air mail Envelopes. Property flown by planes. Men buying Jap rifles. & Bow & arrows. Playing of Softball. Shows in Area. Rain at Gusap.
review_notes: Names troopships Cape Mendocino and David W. Hewes; records March 4 mess hall stove explosion and two P-39 crashes.

pages.title: Observations in Australia & New Guinea (Brisbane, Port Moresby & Gusap)
pages.text: Rations that we got. Race track Ascot. Beer 12 per cent. Steak & eggs & tea. Houses setting up high. Chow poor. Aussie treating Jap. Soldiers caging them up. Natives help allies. Japs force natives to help. Two Kans, pilots Babinsky & Devore. Fox Holes. Shows American productions. S.F. A.P.O. 4873 Stoneman; Brisbane 4873; New Guinea Port Morresby 929.
review_notes: Mentions two fellow Kansas pilots: Babinsky and Devore.

pages.title: Wartime Events, Air Raids & Combat Actions (Feb – Jun 1944)
pages.text: Feb 1944: 20 to 24 Truk island bombed. Berlin bombed and also other cities in Germany, 2000 Airplane Feb 22, Japs being defeated all over S.W.P. Mar 4. 1944 1230: 4 Jap planes attacked. 3 shot down. 3-9-44 to lines. U.S. Troops Invade Hollandia. on 4-22-44. 6-9-44: 17th Sq. Sink 4 destroyers losing 3 B-25's 10 intercepted convoy.
review_notes: Records the 17th Reconnaissance Squadron's June 9, 1944 anti-shipping strike sinking 4 Japanese destroyers.

pages.title: Stateside Summary & New Guinea Camp Impressions
pages.text: July 1942 Rice Calif. Lt. Shirk; Esler Fld. F/O. Thomas; Laurel Lt. Harte; Thomasville. Lt. Nutter; Left 1943 Laurel Oct Train Ride. Natives, Washing Machine Charley. Madam Tojo. Broadcast. Swimming River. Putting up tent Area at Moresby & Gusap. Seeing Wallbays [Wallabies]. Rash. Showers. Aussie soldiers, Aussie planes. Red Cross, Late Mail.
review_notes: Mentions 'Washing Machine Charley' night raiders and 'Madam Tojo' propaganda radio broadcasts.

pages.title: Gusap Operations, Liquor Ration & Aircraft Notes (May – Jul 1944)
pages.text: Gusap: Guys go piggy-back on P-39's. May: We get one qt. of brandy or gin apiece. Aussie planes crack up. B-25 gets food from Townsville. July: get P-39's from Solomons.
review_notes: Describes airmen riding piggy-back inside modified P-39 Airacobras.

pages.title: Arrival on Biak, Air Raid & Switching from P-39s to P-40s (Sep 1944)
pages.text: 9-8-44 Moved from Aitape, Tadji strip. to Biak. Arr 9-8-44. Air Raid on 9-8-44 6 Jap. planes. Biak. Getting seashells. Lots of planes. Dead Japs and caves. Souvenirs of Japs. Coral island. Change Sq. Designation. Sometime in Sept. 1944. Lose Our P-39 & get P-40 Sept 19.
review_notes: Documents transition from P-39 Airacobras to P-40 Warhawks on September 19, 1944.

pages.title: Tadji Strip & Gusap Combat Notes (Feb – Jun 1944)
pages.text: Tadji: Airstrip taken 2 wks before moving up. Japs around 15 miles. Ships in harbor. Us only Air Corps Atalji [at Tadji]. Swimming in ocean. Nice beach & cocoanut groves. Dust fair. Gusap: A-20 crashed killing five. Our 39's having flak from bombs. Bombing & strafing Japs. Very dusty at Tadji. Jelly-fish bites one of our fellows. From Feb 11 to April 30 Gusap hot spot from enemy.
review_notes: Eyewitness notes from Tadji beach and Gusap combat operations.

pages.title: New Guinea Missions, Liberation of Paris & 1944 World Series
pages.text: Our planes take part at Bogadjim. Wewak being bombed when we moved to Tadji. July 29, 1944 P-40 crash close to shore. Aug, 13, Lt. Sharky Crashed at sea, on mission. Paris falls officially 6 P.M. Aug 27, 1944. Browns & Cards play Series 1944. New Designation of Sq. 9-13-44. Cards Win Series 6 games. Cards 4 Browns 2.
review_notes: Logs Lt. Sharky's Aug 13 sea crash, Liberation of Paris (Aug 27, 1944), and the 1944 St. Louis World Series.

pages.title: Biak Crash & Departure for the Philippines (Oct 1944)
pages.text: 1 Japonese matado eye comedo. 10-14-44 Lt. Markoff, Killed at Biak P-40 Crash. Left Biak 10-21-44 6 A.M, Left Hollandia 10-23-44 7 A.M.
review_notes: Includes Spanish note ('1 Japonese matado eye comedo') and Lt. Markoff's Oct 14 fatal P-40 crash.

pages.title: Leyte Air Combat & Cruiser Attack (Nov – Dec 1944)
pages.text: 3 Jap planes shot down. Our P-40's attack Cruiser. 11-11-44. Lt. Marmon missing. 12-1-44.
review_notes: Logs Nov 11, 1944 cruiser strike and Lt. Marmon going missing on Dec 1, 1944.

pages.title: Landing at Leyte & Meeting Filipino Guerrillas (Oct 29, 1944)
pages.text: Left Biak 10-21-44. Landed at Leyte 10-29-44. Storm 65 mi hr. when in Harbor. on 10-29-44. Filipinos come at the ships to trade. Filipino tells how Japs treated them. Took all there cows, pigs, chickens & food. Filipinos already waiting for U.S. troops to land. Some (F) fought with guerrillas. Went to the hills. U.S. send supplies by subs. Filipino talks Eng. fairly good. Filipinos want clothes from soldiers. They trade chickens for shirts & blankets.
review_notes: Written in light pencil; vivid account of landing at Leyte during a 65 mph storm and trading with local Filipinos.

pages.title: Convoy to Leyte, Harbor Air Raids & Unloading on the Beach (Oct – Nov 1944)
pages.text: While on way to Leyte sweating out Jap navy. 10-28-44. While in harbor Japs came over every night. Average of two planes shot down in harbor. 11-4-44 Planes came over. Raid all night. In fox hole. most of night. When off of ship we got on barge. Unloaded on beach. Saw town. Drove around about 3 hrs looking for camp area.
review_notes: Written in light pencil; recounts nightly harbor air raids and spending Nov 4 in a foxhole.

pages.title: Mess Hall Bombing, San Pablo Paratroop Attack & Ormoc Bay Strikes (Nov – Dec 1944)
pages.text: 11-26-44 Had night air raid at 10:30 p.m. Had show in mess hall. Three bombs dropped. One was dud and landed right in camp area. Two bombs exploded. Dud sank 13 ft. One big bomb crater. 12-7-44 Lt. Huber shot down 1 Jap plane. 12-6-44 Have paratroop attack. Take San Pablo strip. At 2300 and taken away by. American troops at 0100 12-7-44. 12-8-44 P-40's sink 2 destroyers and 4 transports.
review_notes: Eyewitness account of Nov 26 mess hall bombing (with 13-ft dud bomb) and Dec 6 Japanese paratroop attack on San Pablo airstrip.

pages.title: Ground Strafing Raid & Squadron Command Change (Dec 1944)
pages.text: 12-14-44 P-40's destroy 20 Jap planes on ground. 12-11-44 Capt. Archuleta assumed command.
review_notes: Logs Capt. Robert Archuleta assuming squadron command on Dec 11, 1944.

pages.title: Troopship Name, Leyte APO & Squadron Aerial Victories (Nov 1944)
pages.text: Filipinos live close in our area. Filipinos do our laundry. 11-6-44 Capt Archuleta, Lt. Johnson, Lt. Regan shot down 1 ea Jap plane. Lt. Marmon got 1 probable. Juan Cabrillo name of Ship. APO Leyte, Dulag. 321. Lt. Rule shot down one Jap plane 11-10-44 Lt. Wells 1 probable. Lt. Denlinger sank one Jap destroyer 11-12-44. 11-29-44 F/O Washatka 2 planes shot down, Lt. Twiggs. 1 plane shot down.
review_notes: Identifies Liberty ship SS Juan Cabrillo and November 1944 aerial victories.

pages.title: Mindoro Convoy Strike & Leyte Departure (Dec 26, 1944 – Jan 9, 1945)
pages.text: Leyte, Town Tacloban, Dulog. First Apo. 320 changed to A.P.O. 72. 12-26-44 21 P-40's attack convoy Jap off coast of Mindoro. 4 pilots missing. 14 planes comeback. 3 crashland. Task Force consisted of 2 battleships, 2 heavy cruisers, 6 destroyers, landing barges. 1-3-44 [1-3-45] pulled away Fr. shore; 4, 5, 6 still on shore Leyte; 7 pulled on LDD to get repairs; 8 out of dry dock. Still in harbor; 9 pulled out of harbor. Joined 100 ship convoy.
review_notes: Details the Dec 26, 1944 Mindoro naval task force attack (where 4 pilots from Page 18 went MIA) and joining the 100-ship Luzon invasion convoy.

pages.title: Lingayen Gulf Assault & Binmaley Landing (Jan 13 – Jan 26, 1945)
pages.text: A.P.O. 70. 1-13-45 at 12 o'clock were Lengayen harbor. From 1-13-45 at noon to 1-14 at night destroyers shelled coast. Knocking out Jap coastal guns. 1-15 an Navy Flier parachuted to safety. Plane crashed on beach. 1-17-45 our convoy was attacked by 6 Jap planes. 5 planes make suicide dives hit two ships. One ship dropped out of convoy. Lst 986 I traveled on. Landed near D+4. No Jap opposition and no raids. 1-20-45 landed Binmaley. Now A.P.O. 70. 1-26-45 Lt. Johnston shot one Jap plane in Luzon.
review_notes: Identifies USS LST-986, kamikaze attack on Jan 17, and landing at Binmaley on Jan 20, 1945.

pages.title: P-51 Mustangs, Medal of Honor Ceremony & FDR's Death (Jan 29 – Apr 13, 1945)
people: Maj. Gen. C. D. Whitehead (Ennis C. Whitehead)
pages.text: 1-29-45 Lt. Hammond shot 1 Jap plane over Luzon. 2-22-45 110th gets P-51's. 3-8-45 Pass to Manila. 3-20-45 Maj G. C. D. Whitehead decorates pilots from 110th & 82nd. 4-2-45 Maj. Gen. Whitehead gives C. D. Medal of Honor to Maj. Shomo 82nd Sq. 4-4-45 17th Sq. Moves to Lengayen, Gp together Again. 4-13-45 Lt. Washatka returns to Sq. 4-12-45 Pres. Roosevelt dies.
review_notes: Records transition to P-51 Mustangs (2-22-45), Maj. William Shomo's Medal of Honor ceremony (4-2-45), and President Roosevelt's death (4-12-45).

pages.title: V-E Day & Start of the Point System Home (Apr 29 – Jun 15, 1945)
pages.text: 4-29-45 10:00 AM Recieved News from Gp. Loud Speaker. Germany Unconditional surrender. Not True. May 1-1945 Hitler supposedly committed suicide. 5-8-45 Germany Unconditional surrender to Allies. Signed at Rhiems, France at 0241 Tues Morning. 5-23-45 Capt. Nolan assumes command. 5-12-45 point system started. 6-15-45 Men Fr. this Sq. going home on point system.
review_notes: Records V-E Day (May 8, 1945), Capt. Nolan assuming command, and start of the point system.

pages.title: Arrival on Ie Shima, Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima & Soviet Entry (Jul 29 – Aug 9, 1945)
pages.text: 7-29-45 At 0700 left Lengayen strip to Ie-Shima arrived at 1200 same day. Island 325 mi from southern Japan. Coral island. Food pretty good. Plenty of rain. Aug. 8, 1945 First Autonic bomb [Atomic bomb] dropped on Hiroshima Honshu island destroyed 60% of Island. Many planes on Ie Shima. Aug 7. B-25 Runs off end of strip exploding killing 5 & 1 seriously injured. Aug 9, 1945 Russians declare war on Japan.
review_notes: Records flight to Ie Shima, news of the Hiroshima atomic bomb, and Soviet declaration of war.

pages.title: Final Air Raid, Last Aerial Victories & Surrender of Japan (Aug 7 – Aug 15, 1945)
pages.text: Aug 7, Jap raid. One bomb dropped destroyed 16 planes. 9 burned. Aug 10 2100 report Jap will surrender providing they can keep the Emperor. The surrender according to Potsdam Ultimatum. Aug. 11 F/O Mulchay shot down one Jap plane over Japan. Aug 14. Maj Nolan shot down 3 Jap planes. Lt. O'Neil shot 1 & Lt. Korypka shot 1. Aug 15 Japan surrender. Our planes called back from mission. First news at 0800 about surrender.
review_notes: Eyewitness account of final August 14 aerial victories and V-J Day surrender news on August 15, 1945.

pages.title: Japanese Surrender Envoys Land on Ie Shima & Point System Orders (Aug 17 – Aug 28, 1945)
pages.text: 8-17-45 Between 0800-1200 a Zero type plane painted white with green crosses was suppose to land Ie Shima carring Japanese envoy to sign peace treaty with MacArthur. Failed to show up. 8-19-45 Two Betty Bomber land with Jap Envoys. Envoys left in C-54 enroute to Manila. Left next day. 8-19 & 21 Go to Okinawa & see Kane & Brown. 8-25-45 Order come thru all men over 85 points to leave for home. Ie-Shima 8-28-45 46 men fly to Manila to go home. Leave by plane early morning.
review_notes: Firsthand eyewitness record of the white Japanese surrender bombers ('Bettys' with green crosses) landing on Ie Shima on Aug 19, 1945.

pages.title: USO Shows, Deactivation of 110th Squadron & Transfer Home (Aug 28 – Oct 8, 1945)
pages.text: 8-28-45 Kay Kyser show at Ie Shima. Shows at 2:30 P.M & 7:30 P.M. 9-2-45 Dick Jurgens & His Marine Orchestra. 9-30-45 110th Tac. Rcn. de-activated. Personnel trfd to 460th Ftr. Sq. 348 Ftr Gp. 10-3-45 Men with 75 points As of Sept 2, 1945 Leave for Okinawa to go home. Men with 80 points and above as of Sept 2, 1945 still not on way home. 10-6-45 Sat. Men 80 points leave for Okinawa. Left area at 1300. Sun 7 just waiting. 10-8-45 Processed the 8th. Trfd. to 380 Bomb Gp.
review_notes: Records Kay Kyser & Dick Jurgens shows, deactivation of 110th Tac. Recon. Sq. (9-30-45), and transfer to 380th Bomb Group on Okinawa.

pages.title: Typhoon Louise on Okinawa & Boarding USS Gen. Bundy (Oct 9 – Oct 21, 1945)
pages.text: 10-9-45. A typhoon hits Okinawa. Many tents blown down. Didn't sleep cause tent down. Stood up practically all night. Next morning, all sacks & baggage all wet. 10-17-45 Called at 1830 to leave next morning at 0700 to board ship. 10-18-45 Thursday At Last Loaded ship at 1645 U.S.S. Gen. Bunday [USS General Omar Bundy]. 10-19-45 Fri: At 1300 pulled out of harbor for the states. 10-20-45 Sat out at sea. Show night. 10-21-45 Sun out at sea. Calm supposedly seen Iwo Jima.
review_notes: Recounts Typhoon Louise on Okinawa (Oct 9) and boarding USS General Omar Bundy (Oct 18) for the voyage home.

pages.title: Pacific Crossing, Diverted to Portland & Arrival at Vancouver Barracks (Oct 22 – Nov 7, 1945)
pages.text: 10-22-45 Mon Sea calm. 10-23-45 Tues Sea little Rough 2 cups ice cream. 10-24-45 Wed Cool winds, Passed ship. 10-25-45 Thrus Cool winds Up to Now Time advanced 4 1/2 hrs. 10-26-45 Fri. At Midnite crossed Date line. 10-26-45 Fri Cool winds. 10-27-45 Sat Navy Day. Cold Winds. 10-28-45 Sun Cloudy. 10-29-45 Mon Destination Portland Instead S.F. 0800 999 Mi. 10-30-45 Tues Cloudy Rough sea. 0800 594. 10-31-45 Wed 0800 274. 11-1-45 Thurs. 11-2-45 Fri out of harbor 0630. No. of ship (AP 152). No. of Mi., 5,700 OKINAWA To S.F. 11-2-45 Fri. off ship At 1800. Vancouver Barracks. At 1600 Band came up river to meet us. Red cross gave us milk, & donoughts. 11-7-45 At. 1900 Leave Vancouver Bks.
review_notes: Documents mid-Pacific diversion to Portland/Vancouver Barracks and welcome band with Red Cross milk and doughnuts.

pages.title: Train to Denver, Honorable Discharge at Fort Logan & Return to Topeka (Nov 7 – Nov 12, 1945)
pages.text: 11-7-45 Board Train. 11-9-45 Arr, Denver At 1900, Ft. Logan. 11-10-45 Still at Logan. Processed. 11-11-45 Discharged at 1630 Sun. 11-12-45 Leave for Topeka.
review_notes: Honourably discharged at Fort Logan, CO on Armistice Day (Sunday, November 11, 1945) and departed for Topeka, KS on Nov 12.

pages.title: Master Overseas Travel & Transit Log (Nov 1943 – Nov 1945)
pages.text: San Francisco 1943 To Brisbane, Aust. Nov 14 To Dec 5: 20 Da. To Port Moresby N.G. Dec 29 To Jan 7 1943: 9 Da. To Gusap N.G. Feb 9 To Feb 9 1944: 2 hrs. To Tadji N.G. June 11 To June 11: 4 hrs. To Biak Sept 8 To Sept 8: 4 hrs. To Leyte, P.I. Oct 20 To Oct 29: 9 da. To Lengayen P.I. Jan 4 To Jan 13 1945 on ship 20: 9 da. To Ie Shima July 29 To July 29: 5 hr. To Okinawa Oct 6 Sat To Oct 6 Sat 1945: 4 hrs. To U.S.A. Oct 19 To Nov: 15 da.
review_notes: Complete leg-by-leg transit duration summary for his entire overseas tour.

pages.text: Cl. 'B' Bond. Series E: 1 Aug. 1944 $7.50 allotment, $10.00 (1) bond, 31 Oct, 1944 Discontinued. 9-2-43 Cl 'F' Almt $22.00 Eff. $25.00 Allotment. Beginning Feb 1-44. Cl. 'A' Bond $1.25 June 1942. Pvt. Jan 6 to 11-15-42; P.F.C. 11-15-42 to 4-1-43; Cpl. 4-1-43 to date: $2,874.80. $13.75 gov't owes me for Bonds. Should have at home (3) $10.00, (1) 25.00.
review_notes: Summarizes exact promotion dates (Pvt, PFC, Cpl), cumulative pay ($2,874.80), and War Bond holdings.
